text: {"headline":"Provider 1000000052 bills 99215 well above risk-adjusted expectation, concentrated on low-complexity patients, but documentation is too thin to confirm or refute upcoding.","leaning":"inconclusive","interpretation":"The claims pattern is consistent with upcoding. The 99215 share is elevated in every complexity stratum, not just among sicker patients, and most 99215s fall on patients with zero or one chronic condition. Sampled examples include upper respiratory infection (C0030577, C0032075), rash (C0031020, C0032580) and follow-up-only visits (C0030705, C0032365) billed at the highest level. The high-complexity 99215s (e.g., C0032106, C0032164) look plausible, so the concern is the low-complexity tail rather than the whole panel. Documentation cannot settle the question: only one 99215 chart came back (C0032370, supported at high MDM with time not recorded), and 4 of the 11 notes claiming moderate-or-higher data reviewed have no lab or test line on the claim, which is weak evidence of cloned or inflated notes, not proof. A reviewer should first request charts for the sampled low-complexity 99215 claims, such as C0030577, C0031020 and C0032686, and check whether the documented MDM and time support the billed level."}
